faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: 'the coil's points straight up' does not say why a quarter cycle becomes a right angle, and 'the readings make the same triangle' skips that the sum of two same-frequency sines is itself a sine, which is what lets its rms be its peak divided by root 2 too.
faults.fix: Say a quarter cycle is a quarter turn of Trigonometry's arm, a right angle, and that the sum of the two waves is itself a sine of the same frequency, so every reading is its wave's peak divided by root 2.

faults.fault: false absolute / a claim that fails in the real world
faults.finding: 'Only the reactance side depends on the frequency ... until on steady DC only R is left' read alone in the dossier is wrong for the capacitor (on DC it blocks) and too strong for a real coil, whose AC resistance rises a little with frequency.
faults.fix: Make it the coil's triangle, say 'in this model', and give the capacitor its own frequency sentence (its side grows as the frequency falls).

faults.fault: the interactive brief shows only the effect, not the cause
faults.finding: The brief names the triangle matching the supply meter but not why the arrows are at right angles.
faults.fix: Name the quarter cycle as the reason inside the brief, within 40 words.

faults.finding: 'Meter across coil or capacitor' is 30 characters, at the limit, and would wrap on a 340 px readout; the three labels are also uneven.
faults.fix: 'Across the resistor', 'Across coil or capacitor', 'Across the supply'.

faults.finding: 'the one Complex numbers lesson 7 wrote as 6 + j8 = 10∠53.13°' says that course used these figures; it used 8 + j6.
faults.fix: 'the triangle of Complex numbers lesson 7's Z = R + jX, here 6 + j8 = 10∠53.13°'.

faults.finding: 'tan φ = X_L ÷ R' then 'for a capacitor it leads' uses the coil's symbol for both.
faults.fix: 'tan φ = X ÷ R, with X the coil's or the capacitor's reactance'.

faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: The reason given for isolating ('cutting a coil's current quickly makes a large back-emf') does not connect to the ohmmeter test.
faults.fix: Isolate and prove dead first; then the kick comes from taking the leads off a large coil while the meter's current flows, so keep clear of the terminals then.

faults.finding: Source 15 is cited only in the numbers list, not in the words.
faults.fix: Footnote the 60 Hz step of the worked example with [^15].

shape.idea named up front: yes, paragraph 1: the readings do not add, the voltages add as arrows at right angles, and dividing by I gives R, X and Z
shape.rule in words: yes: the supply's voltage at each instant is the parts' sum; as arrows a quarter cycle apart, square, add, square root
shape.worked example with real numbers: yes: 12 V, 16 V and 20 V on screen 1; the 30 Ω coil on 230 V in practice; the unknown coil on screen 8
shape.misconception shown failing: yes: the struck-through 28 V bar (screens 1, 4), plain-sum ohms (screen 6), Z taken as X_L and plain-number subtraction (screen 8), four kinds of ohm (screen 10), a negative meter reading (screen 11), the whole Z scaled with frequency (screen 12)
shape.analogy with where it breaks: yes: a cable run round a corner versus the straight line; breaks on space versus time and the capacitor's leg turning the other way
shape.put it into practice: yes: steps with safety first, rule of thumb, worked example, mistakes

verdict: rewrite as draft 2 with the fixes above
